title: Two Planes Bump Into Each Other at Miami Airport
summary:
Two planes bumped into each other on the ground at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, and two people had minor injuries. The crash happened at about 9 p.m. where planes cross paths while moving around the airport.

One plane was a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 carrying 172 people. The other was a UPS Boeing 767 cargo plane, which carries packages instead of passengers. The wingtip of the Copa plane hit the nose of the UPS plane. Photos show a long gash and a bigger hole in its nose.

Investigators say the UPS plane was told to give way to the Copa flight but did not stop, and air traffic control told the pilot he was supposed to yield. The UPS pilot told air traffic control on the radio that he had gone too far at the crossing.

The National Transportation Safety Board, which investigates plane crashes, said the UPS plane had substantial damage. A check of the Copa plane was not finished yet. The safety board has opened an investigation and expects to share a first report within 30 days.
why_it_matters: Knowing how planes stay safe on the ground matters because many kids fly on planes for trips, and careful rules help keep every passenger safe.

keywords.explanation: A cargo plane carries packages and goods instead of people.

background_read: Airports have special roads on the ground called taxiways, where planes move slowly between the runway and the gates, and air traffic controllers tell pilots when to stop and go.
When two planes cross paths on the ground, one pilot is told to give way so the other can pass safely.
The National Transportation Safety Board looks into plane crashes to find out what went wrong and help stop it from happening again.
